Pain medicine · published research

Acute pain

An 830-nm pulsed laser changed Aδ- and C-fiber pain thresholds in healthy volunteers, not clinical pain. Small postoperative studies reported lower early pain after particular surgeries, but these results do not establish efficacy across acute pain conditions.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

An 830-nm pulsed laser changed Aδ- and C-fiber pain thresholds in healthy volunteers, not clinical pain. Small postoperative studies reported lower early pain after particular surgeries, but these results do not establish efficacy across acute pain conditions.

Summary of the Evidence

The database has no standalone Acute pain category. Pain > Nociception contains 14 titles: one healthy-volunteer randomized study, ten coded animal experiments plus two other animal-model reports, one sensory-neuron experiment, and one systematic review. Three narrowly mapped postoperative reports add a hip-arthroplasty trial, a third-molar split-mouth trial, and a retrospective sternotomy cohort. Across these sources there are 17 titles, but the human studies address different procedures rather than one general acute-pain population.

Human and clinical evidence

In a sham-controlled experiment, pulsed 830-nm laser changed Aδ- and C-fiber pain thresholds in healthy adults after one session; this is a sensory response, not relief of clinical acute pain (Takeuchi et al. 2026). After impacted third-molar surgery, a 25-person split-mouth trial reported lower pain, swelling, and trismus on the treated side during the first 48 hours (Le et al. 2022). A small hip-arthroplasty trial and a 264-person retrospective sternotomy cohort also report procedure-specific outcomes (Langella et al. 2018 Wang et al. 2026). Those designs and procedures do not support broad claims.

Animal evidence

Twelve animal reports cover rodents, horses, and leeches, using incisions, inflammation, osteoarthritis-related nociception, and nerve stimulation. Many report reduced nociceptive responses, but the models and behavioral measures differ (Buzza et al. 2024).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

One sensory-neuron study measured metabolism, oxidative stress, mitochondrial potential, and calcium flow. (Zupin et al. 2020).

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The human studies include pulsed 830-nm laser for experimental thresholds and 810-nm laser at 4 J/cm2 after dental surgery. Wavelength is the light's color band and affects tissue penetration. These settings differ by purpose and procedure, so the threshold experiment cannot be used to infer a clinical dose.

Interpretation

The clearest human findings are early postoperative results in defined operations. Evidence for generalized acute pain remains very limited. Future trials should prespecify procedure-specific pain, rescue medication, adverse events, and recovery outcomes.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for short-term pain relief after specific operations in small controlled studies Very low for broad acute pain treatment or for translating sensory-threshold changes into patient pain relief
Publications and records17 titles (14 Pain > Nociception plus 3 mapped postoperative reports)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Human evidence includes one healthy-volunteer experiment and a few small procedure-specific postoperative studies. Their outcomes and designs differ, and they do not test a common acute-pain population. Larger sham-controlled trials should measure pain and analgesic use after defined procedures and assess recovery beyond the first days.
